title: Top OLED TVs for a Cinema-Like Picture (2026)
summary: Tom's Guide and TechRadar both back last year's LG C5 as the sweet spot, with the Samsung S90F for gaming, the Samsung S95F for bright rooms, the LG G5 for peak brightness and the LG B5 as the cheap way into OLED.
method: Picks come from Tom's Guide's best OLED TVs list (updated Aug 7, 2026) and TechRadar's best OLED TVs guide (updated Sep 16, 2026). Each TV here is named by both sites.
assumptions: Prices are what the retailer price boxes on those pages and on Tom's Guide and TechRadar's best TVs lists showed on the day we checked, for the size noted, and they change often. Check the current price on Amazon. The two sites test with different equipment, so brightness and input lag figures are not directly comparable.

products.name: LG C5 OLED
why: TechRadar's best OLED for most people and Tom's Guide's best budget-friendly OLED. Tom's Guide calls it versatile, bright and colorful for movies, shows, games and live sport, and says it is now about half its original price.
Both sites say the newer C6 is only a modest step up, so the C5 is the better buy while it is discounted.
specs: Four HDMI 2.1 ports; 120Hz native, 144Hz with VRR
Dolby Vision, HDR10 and HLG (no HDR10+)
1,180 nits peak in TechRadar's Filmmaker mode test; 9.2ms input lag
products.best_for: Almost anyone who wants a great OLED at a sensible price
products.skip_if: You already own the LG C4, or need HDR10+

products.name: LG C6 OLED
why: TechRadar calls it a considerable upgrade over the C5 thanks to a faster processor, with a crisp picture and effortless motion. Tom's Guide agrees it is fantastic but says the gains are small, apart from a better remote, and not worth about $1,000 more.
TechRadar's price box shows a 65-inch C6 at a big discount, so check the current gap before you decide.
specs: Dolby Vision, HDR10 and HLG (no HDR10+)
1,438 nits peak in TechRadar's Filmmaker mode test; 9.2ms input lag
cons: Glossy screen shows reflections in bright rooms
products.best_for: Buyers who want the newest LG OLED and can get it near the C5's price
products.skip_if: You want to save money, since the C5 is close in performance

products.name: Samsung S90F OLED
why: Tom's Guide's best OLED for console gaming, with near-perfect contrast and Samsung's Gaming Hub that sets up each console and switches to game mode. TechRadar gave it five stars and rates it a great gaming TV, but keeps it out of its main list because of Samsung's panel lottery.
TechRadar's review unit was the 65-inch QD-OLED, and other sizes can use a different panel, so its rating applies to that size.
specs: HDR10, HDR10+ and HLG (no Dolby Vision)
products.best_for: Console and PC gamers who want OLED contrast
products.skip_if: You want Dolby Vision, or need a guaranteed QD-OLED panel in a smaller size

products.name: Samsung S95F OLED
why: TechRadar's pick for bright rooms: vivid colors, high brightness and a glare-free screen that beats reflections. Tom's Guide says it is better than the S90F in most ways but costs far more for fairly minor gains.
TechRadar notes some black crush and slightly raised blacks from the anti-reflection coating.
specs: HDR10, HDR10+ and HLG (no Dolby Vision)
products.best_for: Sunny living rooms where you still want OLED contrast
products.skip_if: You mostly watch in a dark room or want to spend less

products.name: LG G5 OLED
why: TechRadar's best premium OLED, with a four-stack Primary Tandem RGB panel that hit 2,268 nits in Filmmaker mode, then its brightest OLED test. Tom's Guide says it may be one of the best OLEDs ever made.
Tom's Guide still prefers the cheaper LG B6 unless you need one of the brightest TVs it has tested, and TechRadar notes the C5 delivers similar features for much less.
specs: Dolby Vision, HDR10 and HLG (no HDR10+)
9.1ms input lag with Boost mode on
cons: No input select button on the remote
products.best_for: Wall-mounting and bright rooms when you want a top LG panel
products.skip_if: Value matters more than the last bit of brightness

products.name: LG B5 OLED
why: TechRadar's best budget OLED, with vibrant, accurate color, strong contrast and a very low 9.1ms input lag. It is the cheapest way to get an OLED with four HDMI 2.1 ports.
Tom's Guide says the newer LG B6 is a significant step up in performance and still recommends it over the B5, even though the B5 is slightly cheaper now.
specs: Dolby Vision, HDR10 and HLG (no HDR10+)
668 nits peak brightness in TechRadar's test
products.best_for: Dim to moderately lit rooms on a tighter budget
products.skip_if: You can stretch to the LG B6 or C5, or want a bright-room TV
